I want to be free. I want my children to be free. But how can we fight the Roman army?

By using our minds as well as our bodies. We can use guerrilla tactics, strike when they least expect it, and disappear into the shadows. We can use the terrain to our advantage, and we can use our knowledge of the land to avoid their patrols. We may not win every battle, but we can make it too costly for them to pursue us. And in the end, we will emerge victorious.
I'm in. I want to fight for my freedom.
Me too. I'm sick of being a slave.

They are listening to me. They believe in our cause. But we need more. We need more soldiers, more slaves who are willing to fight. I must continue to spread the message, to rally more to our cause. The fight for freedom is not over yet.

setting: The Roman Senate, alarmed by the defeat of the praetorian forces, dispatched a pair of consular legions under the command of Lucius Gellius and Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus Clodianus. The two legions were initially successful but then were defeated by Spartacus. Alarmed at the continued threat posed by the slaves, the Senate charged Marcus Licinius Crassus, the wealthiest man in Rome, with ending the rebellion. Crassus was put in charge of eight legions, numbering upwards of 40,000 trained Roman soldiers. When Spartacus and his followers moved northward again in early 71 BC, Crassus deployed six of his legions on the borders of the region and detached his legate Mummius with two legions to maneuver behind Spartacus. Though ordered not to engage the rebels, Mummius attacked at a seemingly opportune moment but was routed. After this, Crassus's legions were victorious in several engagements, forcing Spartacus farther south through Lucania as Crassus gained the upper hand. By the end of 71 BC, Spartacus was encamped in Rhegium (Reggio Calabria), near the Strait of Messina.

dialogue.content: We have been fighting for too long, and our morale is declining. We need to find a way to turn the tide of this war, or all is lost. Crassus and his armies are too powerful. We cannot defeat him through frontal assaults alone. We need to think of something new, something innovative, something that will catch them off guard. But what? What can we do to defeat the might of Rome?
Spartacus, I offer you one last chance to surrender. Lay down your arms, and your men will be spared.
You know that is not an option, Crassus. We will never surrender. We would rather die free than live as slaves.

Your defiance is admirable, but it will cost you dearly. You are outmatched, outmaneuvered, and soon to be defeated. You have nowhere left to run. Surrender now, and I promise you a quick and painless death.
I cannot surrender. The men trust me to lead them to victory or death. I cannot betray their trust. But what can I do? We are outnumbered and outmatched. We need a miracle.
Spartacus, I have an idea. It is a risky one, but it may be our only chance.
Speak, Laeta. What is your idea?
We have heard that Crassus is using decimation to keep his soldiers in line. What if we could turn that against him? What if we could use it to sow dissent and chaos within his ranks?
Laeta's idea has merit. If we could turn Crassus's own tactics against him, we might be able to weaken his army from within. But how can we do that? How can we make his soldiers turn on him?

I have an idea as well. We could send spies into his camp, disguised as deserters. They could spread rumors and lies, inciting the soldiers against their officers. They could create confusion and discord, weakening the army from within.
Castus, your idea is a good one. But who will go? Who among us can pass for a Roman soldier?
I will go. I have the looks, the language, and the charm to pass as a Roman soldier. I can infiltrate their camp and gather intelligence.
Gannicus is brave, but he is also impulsive. He may not be the best choice for this mission. We need someone who can think on their feet, someone who can improvise, someone like... Agron.
I will go instead. I know the Roman language, and I can blend in with their soldiers. I can gather intelligence and sow dissent, weakening Crassus's army from within.
Agron, you are the best choice for this mission. But be careful. If you are caught, you will be tortured and killed. Are you sure you want to do this?
I am sure, Spartacus. I will do whatever it takes to win this war.
Agron is brave and loyal, but the risks are high. If he is caught, he will be tortured and killed. I cannot let that happen. I must find a way to ensure his safety, to give him a chance to succeed.
Spartacus, I have an idea. What if we create a diversion, something big enough to distract Crassus's army while Agron does his work?
Go on, Saxa. What is your idea?
We could stage a massive attack on one of Crassus's outposts, causing him to divert his troops to defend it. While he is distracted, Agron can move freely within his camp, sowing dissent and chaos.
Saxa's plan is risky, but it may be our only chance. If we can create enough chaos and confusion, we may be able to turn the tide of this war. But we must move quickly and decisively.

Listen, my brothers and sisters. We have a plan, a risky plan, but a plan that may lead us to victory. We will send Agron into Crassus's camp to sow dissent and chaos. While he does his work, we will stage a massive attack on one of Crassus's outposts, causing him to divert his troops. We must move quickly and decisively. Are you with me?
We are with you, Spartacus. To victory or death!

setting: Spartacus sat cross-legged on a woven mat, surrounded by his fellow tribesmen and women. The Thracian banquet was in full swing, and the aroma of roasting meat filled the air. The Maedi tribe had gathered together to celebrate their history and culture, and Spartacus was eager to partake in the festivities. He had spent much of his life as a soldier and gladiator, fighting for the entertainment of others. But here, among his own people, he felt a sense of belonging that he had not experienced in many years. The fire crackled in the center of the room, casting flickering shadows on the walls. It was a warm, welcoming atmosphere, and Spartacus was glad to be a part of it.

dialogue.content: As he listened to his fellow tribespeople speaking, Spartacus felt a sense of pride in his heritage. He had always known that he was a Thracian, but he had never fully understood what that meant until now. The Maedi tribe was a fierce and independent people, and they had a rich cultural history that dated back centuries. Spartacus was determined to learn as much as he could about his roots, so that he could pass that knowledge down to future generations.

The Maedi people have always been warriors," the elder said, his voice deep and resonant. "We have fought many battles, both to defend our land and to expand our territory. But we are not just fighters. We are also a people of great skill and ingenuity. Our craftsmen are renowned throughout the region for their metalwork and pottery.

I remember when I was a boy," one of the hunters said, his eyes sparkling with nostalgia. "My father took me hunting in the forest. We tracked a deer for hours, until we finally caught it. It was a moment of great pride for me, to know that I was able to provide for my family.

I too have hunted many times," Spartacus said, his voice quiet but firm. "But my life has taken a different path. I have fought in battles, and I have entertained crowds as a gladiator. But I have always felt that there was more to life than that. Here, among my own people, I feel that I have found a sense of purpose that I have been searching for.
And we are glad to have you here, Spartacus," the weaver said, a warm smile on her face. "You may not have grown up with us, but you are still one of us. We are all Maedi, and we stand together.

As he looked around the room, Spartacus felt a sense of belonging that he had not experienced in many years. He had been a slave for so long, forced to fight and entertain for the pleasure of others. But here, among his own people, he was free. He was a Thracian, and he was proud of it.

There is something else you should know, Spartacus," the elder said, his voice grave. "The Romans are encroaching on our land. They have already taken over several nearby villages, and we fear that they will soon come for us. We must be prepared to fight.
I am ready to fight," Spartacus said, his eyes flashing with determination. "I have fought against the Romans before, and I know their tactics. We can defeat them if we stand together.
But we are not as organized as the Roman army," the hunter said, his brow furrowed in concern. "We do not have the same training or equipment.

We may not have their training or equipment," Spartacus said, his voice rising in passion. "But we have something that they do not. We have the spirit of the Maedi people. We have the courage and the determination to fight for what is ours. And we will not let the Romans take that away from us.
Then we stand with you, Spartacus," the weaver said, her voice steady. "We will fight for our land and our people. And we will not be defeated.

As he looked around the room, Spartacus felt a sense of pride and gratitude that he had never experienced before. These were his people, and they were willing to fight and die for each other. He knew that the battle ahead would be difficult, but he also knew that they could win if they stood together. The fire crackled in the center of the room, casting a warm glow on the faces of the Maedi tribe. It was a moment of unity and strength, and Spartacus was honored to be a part of it.

setting: The battlefield was chaotic, with the clash of swords and screams of agony filling the air. Spartacus stood at the forefront of his remaining soldiers, his face grim and determined. The rebels were vastly outnumbered by the oncoming legions, but Spartacus refused to back down. He knew this was their last stand, and he was willing to sacrifice himself to ensure the escape of his soldiers. The sun was setting, casting an eerie light upon the scene, and the air was thick with the smell of blood and death.

dialogue.content: I knew this day would come. I knew that our rebellion would eventually come to this bloody end. But I will not let my soldiers die in vain. I will not let the Romans celebrate their victory over us. I will fight until my last breath, and if necessary, I will give up my life for the freedom of my people.
Spartacus! Surrender now and we will show mercy to your remaining soldiers.
Mercy? You speak of mercy after you have slaughtered countless innocent people? You are no better than the beasts of the wild. I will never surrender to the likes of you.
Spartacus, we cannot hold them off for much longer. We need to retreat now!
I will not leave anyone behind. We retreat together, or we die together. That is our only option now.
But what about you, Spartacus? You cannot stay here and fight alone.
I will buy you all the time you need to escape. Go now, while you still can.

Brothers, today we fight for our freedom. Today, we stand together against our oppressors. Do not fear death, for it is only through death that we can truly be free. Let us show these Romans what it means to be a warrior of the people!
This is it. This is how it ends. But I will not die in vain. I will die as a warrior, as a leader, and as a symbol of hope for my people. May they never forget the sacrifices we made for our freedom.
I am Spartacus, and I will always be Spartacus.

setting: Spartacus and his commanders are gathered in the center of the camp, surrounded by tents and makeshift shelters. The sun is high in the sky, indicating that it is midday. The atmosphere is tense and serious, as everyone knows that the upcoming battle will be their last chance to escape the might of the Roman army. Spartacus stands in the center, his eyes scanning the faces of his commanders, looking for any signs of fear or hesitation. The commanders stand in a semi-circle around him, each one holding a map or scroll with information about the enemy's movements and plans.

dialogue.content: This battle will be our last chance. We cannot afford to lose. I must prepare my troops and ensure that they are ready for anything. I will not let them die in vain. I must devise a plan that will give us the best chance of victory.
We cannot wait any longer, Spartacus. We must attack now while the Romans are still separated.
I agree. We cannot let them regroup and come at us with full force.
I understand your concerns, but we need to be smart about this. We cannot simply charge in and hope for the best. We need to have a plan.
What plan do you suggest, Spartacus? We are vastly outnumbered.
He is right. We are outnumbered, but we have the advantage of knowing the terrain and being more familiar with our surroundings. If we can use this to our advantage, we may be able to turn the tide.
We will lure them into a trap. We will use the hills to our advantage and create a false retreat. When they follow us, we will turn and attack them from behind.
How will we ensure that they follow us?
We will send a small group to attack them and then retreat. This will lead them to believe that we are weaker than we are and that they can easily defeat us.
That's a risky move, Spartacus. What if they don't fall for it?
He is right. It is a risk, but it is one that we must take. We have no other choice.
We have no other choice. We must take this risk if we are to have any chance of victory. I have faith in our troops. They will not let us down.
What about our wounded? We cannot leave them behind.
We will tend to our wounded and make sure that they are safe. We cannot afford to leave anyone behind.

I must remain strong for my troops. I cannot let them see any sign of weakness. If they see that I am afraid, they will lose faith in me and in our cause. I must show them that I am confident and that we will emerge victorious.
Prepare the troops. We attack at dawn.

setting: Spartacus and his generals are gathered in the countryside, preparing for their next battle against the Romans. They stand in a circle, discussing their plan of attack. Spartacus, the leader of the rebellion, stands tall and resolute, his eyes scanning the faces of his comrades. Crixus, his trusted advisor, stands to his left, his arms crossed and his brow furrowed in concentration. The other generals, a mix of former slaves and experienced fighters, stand around them, listening intently to their leader's words. The sun beats down on them, casting long shadows across the grassy plain, as they debate the best way to defeat the might of Rome.

dialogue.content: We have come so far, but there is still so much to do. The Romans have underestimated us from the beginning, thinking us nothing but slaves and criminals. But we have shown them what we are capable of, and we will not stop until we have won our freedom. I must be careful with my words, though. These men look to me for guidance, and I cannot afford to make mistakes. Our plan must be foolproof, or we risk losing everything we have fought for.

We cannot simply charge at them head-on. The Romans will be prepared for that, and we will be cut down like lambs to the slaughter. We need to be strategic, to use our knowledge of the land to our advantage.
But what if we split up our forces? We could attack them in two places at once, divide their attention and their strength.
Or we could lure them into a trap. Make them think they have the upper hand, then strike when they least expect it.

I hear your ideas, and they have merit. But we must remember that the Romans have superior numbers and training. We cannot afford to make mistakes. We need a plan that is both bold and cautious, one that will catch them off guard but also minimize our losses.

Perhaps we could use our knowledge of the local terrain to our advantage. If we can lure them into a narrow pass or a dense forest, we could use our superior knowledge of the land to outmaneuver them.

Crixus is right. We need to use every advantage we have, even if it means taking risks. But we must also be careful not to underestimate the Romans. They are a formidable enemy, and they will not hesitate to crush us if we give them the chance. I must tread carefully.
I have an idea. We could use our herdsmen and shepherds to our advantage. They know this land better than anyone, and they can help us navigate the countryside without being detected.
Or we could use our Celts and Gauls to our advantage. They are fierce warriors, and their knowledge of guerrilla warfare could give us the edge we need.

These are all excellent suggestions. But we must choose carefully. Our plan must be decisive, and we cannot afford to waste any more time. We must strike soon, before the Romans have a chance to regroup.
I suggest we split our forces into three groups. One group will attack from the north, one from the south, and one from the east. This will divide their attention and give us the element of surprise.

That could work. But we must also be prepared for the possibility of failure. We cannot afford to lose any more of our fighters. We must make sure that everyone knows their role and that we are all working together.
What about supplies? We cannot sustain a prolonged battle without food and water. We must make sure that we have enough resources to last us through the fight.
I agree. We will need to gather as many supplies as we can before we launch our attack. We cannot afford to leave anything to chance.

This is it. Our plan is set, and we are ready to face the might of Rome once again. I can feel the weight of responsibility on my shoulders, but I am ready for it. We will fight with everything we have, and we will not stop until we have won our freedom.

setting: Spartacus stands before his army, bloodied and bruised, with the Roman army encamped around them. They are cut off from their supplies and under siege at Rhegium. He delivers a rousing speech to his men, urging them to fight to the death against the Roman army.

dialogue.content: My brothers, we stand here today, surrounded by the might of the Roman army. We are cut off from our supplies, besieged and outnumbered. But I tell you, my brothers, that we are not defeated. We are Spartacus! We are free men who will not be caged! We will not bow down to the chains of our oppressors! We will fight, and we will die if we must, but we will go down fighting! For our freedom! For our dignity! For our lives! We will not surrender! We will not give up! We will fight to the last man! And when we fall, we will fall as free men! As men who refused to be broken! As men who chose death over slavery!
But how can we fight, Spartacus? We are outnumbered and outmatched!

We may be outnumbered, but we are not outmatched. We are warriors, my brothers! We have fought and bled together! We have faced the might of the Roman army and lived to tell the tale! And we will do it again! We will not be intimidated by their numbers. We will not be cowed by their weapons! We will stand together, as brothers, and we will fight! We will use every weapon at our disposal. We will use our swords, our spears, our shields. We will use our courage, our strength, our determination. And we will show the Roman army what it means to face free men!
But what about our families? Our loved ones? We cannot leave them to the mercy of the Romans!

I understand your fears, my brothers. I too have loved ones who are suffering under the yoke of Roman oppression. But we cannot let our fear paralyze us. We cannot let our love for our families blind us to the cause we fight for. We fight for their freedom, as well as ours. We fight for a world where our children can live in peace and prosperity. We fight for a world where no man or woman is enslaved or oppressed. And we will win this fight, my brothers. We will win this fight, or we will die trying. But we will not surrender! We will not give up! We will fight until our dying breaths!
But what about Crassus, Spartacus? He is a ruthless man, and he has us trapped here.

Crassus. The name brings back memories of a man who was as cunning as he was ruthless. A man who was not afraid to use any means necessary to achieve his goals. A man who had shown no mercy to those who stood in his way. But I am Spartacus. And I will not be intimidated by him. I will not let him break me. I will not let him break my brothers.

Crassus may be a ruthless man, my brothers. But he is not invincible. He is a man, just like us. And he has weaknesses, just like us. We will find those weaknesses, and we will exploit them. We will use our knowledge of the terrain, our knowledge of his tactics, and our knowledge of his weaknesses to defeat him. We will not let him crush us under his boot. We will fight, and we will win!
But what about the pirates, Spartacus? They betrayed us. They left us stranded here. How can we trust anyone?

The pirates. The memory of their treachery still burns in my mind. I had trusted them, and they had betrayed me. They had taken our money and left us stranded here. But I cannot let their treachery break my spirit. I cannot let their betrayal destroy my faith in humanity. I must find a way to keep my faith alive, to keep my hope burning bright.

The pirates may have betrayed us, my brothers. But we cannot let their treachery destroy our faith in humanity. There are still good people in this world, people who will stand with us, people who will fight for our cause. We must find those people, my brothers. We must find those who share our vision of a better world. We must find those who are willing to stand with us, even in the face of adversity. And we will find them, my brothers. We will find them, and we will fight together, as brothers, until we are free!

setting: The setting is a Roman prison where two prisoners are debating whether to join Spartacus' rebellion or not. This takes place during a time when the legions of Pompey have returned from Hispania and were ordered by the Senate to head south to aid Crassus. Crassus, who is leading the Roman army, fears that Pompey's involvement would deprive him of credit for defeating Spartacus himself. Hearing of Pompey's involvement, Spartacus tried to make a truce with Crassus, but he refused. Spartacus and his army then broke through the Roman fortifications and headed to Brundusium with Crassus's legions in pursuit.

dialogue.content: I need to convince these prisoners to join my cause. With each new recruit, our army grows stronger, and our chances of victory increase. But I must also be careful not to reveal too much information about our plans. These prisoners are still loyal to Rome, and I don't want to risk them betraying us.
Why should we join your rebellion? We have a chance to be pardoned if we stay loyal to Rome.

Think about it. What has Rome done for you? You're rotting away in this prison, and for what? For the crime of being poor or standing up against the corrupt elite? Join me, and together we can fight for our freedom and for a better future for all of us.
But what about the Roman army? They're powerful, and they have the backing of the Senate. How can we possibly win?

I won't lie to you, the road ahead will be difficult. But we have something they don't: the will to fight for our freedom. We are fighting for something greater than ourselves. And if we work together, we can overcome any obstacle.
What about Crassus? He's the one leading the Roman army, right? He's known for his brutality and cunning.
Crassus may be a formidable opponent, but he is not invincible. We have a plan to defeat him, but I cannot reveal it here. Join us, and you will see for yourself.
I don't know. I'm not sure if I'm ready to risk my life for this.

Think about what you have to gain. Freedom, a chance to make a difference, and a place in history. Do not let fear hold you back from achieving greatness. Join us, and we will fight for a better future for all of us.
What happens if we lose? What if we're caught?

I won't lie to you, the consequences could be severe. But I assure you, we will do everything in our power to avoid capture. And if we do get caught, we will face our fate with bravery and honor, knowing that we fought for what we believed in.
I...I think I'm ready to join you. What do I need to do?
Welcome to the rebellion, brother. We will need your strength and courage in the battles ahead. We will provide you with weapons and training, and together we will fight for our freedom.
I...I'll join too. I can't just sit here and do nothing while others fight for a better future.
Good. Together, we will overcome any obstacle and achieve greatness. Join me, and let us fight for our freedom!

setting: Spartacus and his army hold a funeral service to honor fallen soldiers who died fighting for their freedom. The rebel camp is somber, with a few torches illuminating the area. The ground is damp from the recent rain, and the wind is blowing softly, carrying the smell of burning wood and incense. Spartacus stands at the center of the camp, surrounded by his fellow rebels, who are gathered to pay their respects to their fallen comrades.

dialogue.content: The weight of this war is heavy on my shoulders. I never wanted to lead a rebellion, but I had no choice. The Romans left us with no other option. They treated us like animals, and we had to fight for our freedom. I am proud of what we have accomplished so far, but the cost has been high. So many of our brothers and sisters have died in this fight. Today, we honor their sacrifice.

Today, we gather to mourn our fallen brothers and sisters. They gave their lives for our cause, and we will never forget their sacrifice. We will honor their memory by continuing to fight for our freedom. We will not rest until every slave is free from Roman tyranny.
Our fallen brothers and sisters will be remembered as heroes. They fought with bravery and determination, and their sacrifice will not be in vain.
Today, we mourn their loss, but tomorrow, we will continue their fight. We will not stop until every slave is free, and every Roman is brought to justice.
Our brothers and sisters died so that we could live as free men and women. We will honor their memory by never giving up on our cause.
May their souls rest in peace, and may we continue to fight for their legacy. We will never forget their sacrifice.

I must remain strong for my people. They look up to me, and I cannot let them down. But sometimes, I wonder if we will ever truly be free. The Romans are powerful, and they will not give up without a fight. But I cannot let my doubts show. I must lead with confidence and determination.
Let us take a moment of silence to honor our fallen brothers and sisters.
Thank you all for coming. Our fallen brothers and sisters will always be remembered as heroes. Let us continue their fight with renewed strength and determination.

setting: The gladiator barracks were filled with the sounds of men preparing for battle. Spartacus, the Thracian gladiator who had led a successful slave rebellion against the Roman Republic, stood at the center of the room, surrounded by his fellow fighters. They were all battle-hardened and ready to fight for their freedom, but Spartacus could sense the tension in the air. He knew that their victory was not guaranteed, but he refused to let his men see any doubt in his eyes. Spartacus raised his voice, announcing their upcoming battle and predicting their inevitable victory.

Spartacus led his men into battle against the Roman legions, fighting with all their strength and skill. The battle was fierce, and the outcome was uncertain until the very end. In the end, the slaves emerged victorious, but at a great cost. Many of their comrades had fallen, and Spartacus himself had sustained a mortal wound. As he lay dying, surrounded by his fellow fighters, he knew that his legacy would live on.

dialogue.content: I must remain confident, despite the odds. My men look to me for guidance, and I cannot afford to show any weakness. We have come this far, and we will not stop until we have achieved our freedom. The Roman Republic may have underestimated us, but they will soon learn that we are not to be trifled with. Victory is within our grasp, and I will do whatever it takes to ensure that we succeed.
Spartacus, have you considered the risks of this battle? The Roman legions outnumber us ten to one. Even the greatest warriors can fall in battle, and we cannot afford to lose our leader.

I am aware of the risks, Crixus. But we have no choice but to fight. We cannot go back to slavery. We must stand and fight for our freedom. I have faith in our men and in our cause. We will emerge victorious.
Spartacus, what do you plan to do if we win this battle? Will we continue to fight against the Republic, or will we be satisfied with our freedom?
Gannicus raises an important question. Our ultimate goal is freedom, but what will we do once we achieve it? The Republic will not simply let us go free. We must have a plan for what comes next.

Our fight does not end with this battle. Even if we win, the Republic will not simply let us go free. We must have a plan for what comes next. We will continue to fight until every slave is free, and the Republic is brought to its knees.
Spartacus, what if we do not win this battle? What if we are defeated?

We cannot afford to think like that, Castus. We must fight with all of our might, with every ounce of strength we possess. We must believe in ourselves and in our cause. We are not fighting for ourselves alone. We are fighting for every slave who has ever been held in chains. Failure is not an option.

My friends, my brothers in arms. I am dying, but our fight is not over. You must continue to fight for our cause, for our freedom. The Republic will not let us go free, but we will fight until every slave is free. Remember what we have fought for, what we have died for. Our legacy will live on, and our cause will never die.
Spartacus, we will continue to fight in your name. We will never forget what you have done for us, and for all slaves.
Spartacus, you have shown us what it means to be truly free. We will carry on your legacy, and we will fight for our freedom until the end of our days.
Spartacus, you have given us hope, and you have shown us that we are not alone in our struggle. We will honor your memory by continuing to fight for our freedom.

setting: Spartacus and his army of slaves had taken refuge in the southern Italian city of Thurii, where they had won several battles against the Roman army. However, Spartacus and his men were not content with simply defending their stronghold. They wanted to take the fight to Rome itself, to bring the city to its knees and free all the slaves within its walls. And so, they marched north, towards the heart of the Roman Empire. As they reached the outskirts of Rome, Spartacus ordered his men to prepare for an assault on the city walls.

dialogue.content: This is it. This is the moment we've been waiting for. We've come so far, fought so hard, and now we stand at the gates of Rome itself. The city that has enslaved us for so long, that has treated us like animals, that has taken everything from us - our families, our homes, our freedom. But we will not be defeated. We will not be broken. We will fight until our last breath, until every last one of us is free. This is our destiny.
Ready the archers! Keep them at bay!
Brace yourselves, men! They're coming!
Charge! Take the walls!

This is madness. The odds are against us, the enemy is relentless, and every moment we fight is a moment closer to our deaths. But we have come too far to turn back now. This is our moment of glory, our chance to strike a blow against the oppressors who have held us down for so long. I will not back down, I will not surrender. I will fight until my last breath, until every last one of my men is free.
Fall back! Regroup at the gate!
We can't let them breach the walls! Hold the line!
Push forward! We can do this!

This is not going as planned. We've been fighting for hours, and still we have not broken through their defenses. Our men are tired, hungry, and thirsty, and the Romans are still coming at us with everything they've got. I fear that this may be the end for us. That we may die here, on the walls of Rome, with nothing to show for our struggle.
Crassus is on his way! We just need to hold out a little longer!
We've got them on the run! Keep pushing!
No! We can't give up now! We need to keep fighting, keep pushing forward, until we break through their defenses and take the city!

It's over. We've lost. I can feel it in my bones. The Romans have beaten us, and now they will make us pay for our defiance. But I will not go down without a fight. I will take as many of them with me as I can. I will show them that we are not just slaves, not just animals to be beaten and broken. We are human beings, with hearts and souls and a burning desire for freedom. And we will never give up, never surrender. Even in death, we will triumph over our oppressors.
Freedom...will never...die...
